The voice AI sector is hot, and top players are trying to consolidate their position as more business models come to the fore through partnerships and acquisitions. Deepgram is the latest to make such moves: The company said on Thursday that it is acquiring Daily, the maker and maintainer of one of the most popular open-source voice AI infrastructures, Pipecat.

The companies didn’t disclose the deal amount but said that they will keep Pipecat open-source.

For the uninitiated, Pipecat is a framework that manages voice and video streams along with other pieces in the pipeline, like speech-to-text (STT), large language models, and text-to-speech (TTS) models while reducing latency. Its maker, Daily, provides hosted infrastructure for voice and video calls of any kind.

With Pipecat, Deepgram will likely gain a deeper understanding of real-time voice and video infrastructure.

Daily has raised over $62 million in funding to date from investors such as Tiger Global, Highfield Capital, Nat Friedman, Lachy Groom and Kevin Weil, according to PitchBook data. Earlier this year, Deepgram reached unicorn status with a $130 million Series C round. Incidentally, both companies were in the same Y Combinator batch in 2016.

Kwindla Kramer, Daily’s co-founder, said around the time when GPT-4 came out, the company started experimenting with AI-to-human communication over voice and text, which eventually resulted in the Pipecat framework. He noted that while there has been a lot of acquisition interest, he favored Deepgram’s CEO Scott Stephenson’s commitment to keeping Pipecat open-source forever, and the engineering culture of both organizations matched, giving Daily’s team the freedom to work on different parts of the stack within a bigger organization.

“Scott was super committed to Pipecat being open-source and vendor-neutral forever. I think there is both a personal commitment and commercial driver there. If you sit in the middle of an ecosystem that’s growing very fast, and have many parts of that ecosystem that are genuinely the best from your company, then everything being as open as possible is like a commercial advantage,” Kramer told TechCrunch.

Stephenson said that Deepgram has been wanting to work in open source for a long time, and the company realized that an orchestration framework for agents was a potential area, which drove the decision to partner with Daily.

“We want to open up the ecosystem so everybody can build voice agents. It’s great if you’re using Deepgram models, but I want you to be using the best models for your use case. And if Deepgram notices that we have some ground to catch up on in a certain area for our own models and products, that’s great. We want you to use partners, and then we’ll also work on becoming better in those areas,” he said.

Stephenson said the acquisition lets developers build agents with expressivity and end-to-end speech systems by plugging in different models and a context bus that connects all parts.

For Deepgram, the deal also lets it explore areas beyond voice through Pipecat, as the framework caters to real-time communication in different formats.

“We never thought about Pipecat as a voice toolkit. We thought about it as the toolkit we needed to build this new kind of AI-native software. Because of where we came from, we just always assumed real-time,” Kramer said.

Deepgram is also launching Real-Time Context Standard (RCS), an open protocol for voice agents that it co-developed with the Pipecat team. The protocol defines metadata like context from the audio, like a whisper, instructions for a language model on how it can use those signals, and guidance on how the response should sound.

Voice AI has seen a lot of investment from both the model and the infrastructure sides. Model makers like ElevenLabs, Gradium, and Fish Audio have raised millions of dollars. On the other hand, infrastructure companies like LiveKit and Vapi have raised multi-million-dollar funding rounds this year.

translation.html:
语音 AI 行业正热，随着更多商业模式涌现，头部企业正试图通过合作与收购巩固自身地位。Deepgram 是最新采取此类行动的公司：该公司周四表示，将收购 Daily。Daily 是 Pipecat 的开发者和维护者，Pipecat 是最受欢迎的开源语音 AI 基础设施之一。

两家公司没有披露交易金额，但表示将保持 Pipecat 开源。

对于不熟悉 Pipecat 的人来说，这是一个管理语音和视频流的框架，同时还管理处理流程中的其他组件，例如语音转文本（STT）、大语言模型和文本转语音（TTS）模型，并降低延迟。其开发公司 Daily 为各种语音和视频通话提供托管基础设施。

借助 Pipecat，Deepgram 可能会对实时语音和视频基础设施有更深入的了解。

根据 PitchBook 的数据，Daily 迄今已从 Tiger Global、Highfield Capital、Nat Friedman、Lachy Groom 和 Kevin Weil 等投资者处筹集了超过 6200 万美元的资金。今年早些时候，Deepgram 通过一轮 1.3 亿美元的 C 轮融资跻身独角兽行列。巧合的是，两家公司都参加了 Y Combinator 2016 年的同一期创业加速项目。

Daily 联合创始人 Kwindla Kramer 表示，在 GPT-4 发布前后，公司开始尝试让 AI 通过语音和文字与人交流，最终催生了 Pipecat 框架。他指出，虽然有很多公司表达过收购意向，但他更看重 Deepgram 首席执行官 Scott Stephenson 关于让 Pipecat 永久保持开源的承诺，而且两家公司的工程文化契合，Daily 团队可以在一个更大的组织中自由地开发技术栈的不同部分。

“Scott 非常坚定地承诺，让 Pipecat 永远保持开源和厂商中立。我认为，这既有个人承诺，也有商业动因。如果你处于一个快速发展的生态系统的中心，而这个生态系统中许多真正最好的组件都来自你的公司，那么让一切尽可能开放就会成为一种商业优势，”Kramer 告诉 TechCrunch。

Stephenson 表示，Deepgram 长期以来一直希望参与开源工作，公司意识到智能体编排框架是一个有潜力的方向，这促使其决定与 Daily 合作。

“我们希望开放这个生态系统，让每个人都能构建语音智能体。如果你使用 Deepgram 的模型，那很好，但我希望你使用最适合自己应用场景的模型。如果 Deepgram 发现，我们自己的模型和产品在某个领域还有需要追赶的地方，那也很好。我们希望你使用合作伙伴的产品，同时我们也会努力在这些领域做得更好，”他说。

Stephenson 表示，此次收购让开发者能够通过接入不同的模型，以及一个连接所有组件的上下文总线，构建具有丰富表达能力的智能体和端到端语音系统。

对 Deepgram 而言，这笔交易也使其能够通过 Pipecat 探索语音以外的领域，因为该框架支持不同形式的实时通信。

“我们从未把 Pipecat 看作一个语音工具包。我们把它看作构建这种新型 AI 原生软件所需的工具包。由于我们的业务背景，我们一直默认它应该是实时的，”Kramer 说。

Deepgram 还将推出实时上下文标准（Real-Time Context Standard，RCS），这是其与 Pipecat 团队共同开发的语音智能体开放协议。该协议定义了元数据，例如音频中的上下文信息（如耳语），还定义了语言模型如何使用这些信号的指令，以及回复应以何种声音方式呈现的指导信息。

语音 AI 的模型和基础设施两端都获得了大量投资。ElevenLabs、Gradium 和 Fish Audio 等模型开发商已筹集数百万美元。另一方面，LiveKit 和 Vapi 等基础设施公司今年也完成了数百万美元的融资。
